message.content:
For a **fair** two‑sided coin each flip has only two equally likely outcomes:

| Outcome | Probability |
|---------|-------------|
| Head    | \( \frac{1}{2}\) |
| Tail    | \( \frac{1}{2}\) |

So the probability of landing on heads in one independent toss is  

\[
P(\text{Head})=\frac{\text{Number of favorable outcomes}}{\text{Total possible outcomes}}
               =\frac{1}{2}=0.50 .
\]

If the coin were known to be *biased*, you would replace “\(1/2\)” with whatever bias value was given (e.g., \(p\)). But under normal assumptions—an unbiased coin—the chance of a head is exactly ½.
